Chili’s Steak Fajitas Recipe

By Stephanie Manley Updated 08/9/26
Jump to Recipe
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 13:47
Instaread

The sizzling platter of steak, peppers, and onions is one of the most recognizable moments on a Chili’s menu. This copycat version starts with skirt steak soaked in a soy-lime marinade, then seared hot and paired with sautéed peppers and onions. The marinade develops the same umami-rich, slightly sweet flavor Chili’s is known for, and a quick sear keeps the beef tender rather than chewy. It’s an easy centerpiece for a weeknight dinner or a build-your-own fajita bar when friends come over.

This Chili’s Steak Fajitas recipe recreates the restaurant’s sizzling platter using skirt steak, a cut prized for its beefy flavor and tenderness when sliced against the grain. The beef soaks overnight in a marinade of soy sauce, Worcestershire, lime, garlic, and brown sugar before a fast sear in a screaming-hot skillet.

While the steak marinates, the onions and bell peppers get their own quick soak in a lighter version of the same marinade, then a short sauté so they stay crisp-tender rather than mushy. Everything comes together on warm flour tortillas with Colby Jack cheese, sour cream, pico de gallo, and lime wedges so everyone can build their own plate.

Why you should try making Chili’s Steak Fajitas at home

The sizzling platter of beef strips, peppers, and onions always draws attention at Chili’s. While this homemade version may not have the same dramatic entrance, the taste is even better. Tender skirt steak soaks up a rich marinade, then a quick sear over high heat is all it takes. Serve the beef with sautéed peppers and onions, and let your guests build their own fajitas with toppings like Colby Jack, sour cream, and Pico de Gallo. This Chili’s Steak Fajitas recipe delivers restaurant-quality food right from your kitchen.

Ingredients and their roles in this recipe

For the beef, you’ll need:

  • Skirt steak –  is the perfect cut because it’s beefy yet tender, especially when cut across the grain. Use outside skirt steak if you can find it, but inside skirt steak is more widely available and is a good option.
  • Soy sauce – provides a salty, umami-rich flavor and gives the meat a beautiful color.
  • Worcestershire sauce – bumps up the umami flavor and adds a touch of sweetness along with notes of savory fermentation.
  • Fresh lime juice – brightens the marinade with citrus flavors that are less harsh than lemons.
  • Garlic, finely chopped – adds a degree of sharpness and aromatic elements to the beef.
  • Light brown sugar – sweetens the marinade, adds flavor, and promotes even caramelization.

For the peppers and onions, you’ll need:

  • Sweet yellow onion, large – caramelizes for a touch of sweetness that works well with the bell peppers.
  • Red bell pepper – the sweetest bell pepper, with a bit of fruity tang and a dash of color.
  • Green bell pepper – more earthy and bitter than red or orange bell peppers.
  • Orange bell pepper – sits between green and red bell peppers in ripeness. It has a more noticeable color and a bit of citrus flavor.
  • Neutral oil (such as vegetable or avocado) – cooks the peppers and onions without adding additional flavors.
  • Water – creates steam to soften the veggies and helps to remove the fond from the bottom of the pan.
  • Soy sauce – seasons the vegetables and adds a boost of umami flavor.
  • Worcestershire – adds even more umami and fruitiness.
  • Lime juice – contrasts with the richness of the umami and salt to brighten the vegetables.

To serve Chili’s Steak Fajitas, you’ll need:

  • Flour tortillas – serve as the base for the dish. They are softer and have a milder flavor than corn tortillas.
  • Cooked beef – has a savory flavor and is the main protein for the dish.
  • Peppers and onions – offer a sweet and earthy balance to the beef.
  • Colby Jack cheese, shredded – adds a mild, creamy richness and melts well.
  • Sour cream – contributes tang and a touch of coolness.
  • Pico de Gallo (see below for the Chili’s version) – moistens the beef and peppers while adding a fresh tomato flavor.
  • Lime wedges – add more acidity and help to cut through the heavier toppings.

Ingredient Notes

  • Use outside skirt steak when you can find it; it’s more tender than inside skirt steak, though both work in this recipe.
  • Squeeze fresh limes rather than using bottled juice. Bottled lime juice has a duller, slightly metallic flavor that comes through in the marinade.
  • Slice the onion and bell peppers to a similar half-inch thickness so they cook at the same rate.

How to make Chili’s Fajitas at home

To marinate the steak:

  1. In a large mixing bowl or a self-sealing food-safe bag, mix the soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, fresh lime juice, chopped garlic, and brown sugar until the sugar dissolves.
  2. Trim any fat and gristle from the skirt steak, then place it in the marinade.
  3. Turn the steak to coat evenly, cover the bowl or seal the bag, and chill for 8 to 12 hours. Flip halfway through.

To prepare the vegetables:

  1. About two hours before cooking, slice the onion and bell peppers into half-inch-thick strips. Place them in a mixing bowl or self-sealing food-safe bag.
  2. Add the neutral oil, water, soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce to the bowl or bag. Massage the vegetables to coat them with the marinade, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to two hours.

To cook the steak:

  1. Remove the steaks from the marinade and pat them dry with a paper towel.
  2. Place the steaks on a plate for 30 minutes to come up to room temperature.
  3. During the last 10 minutes of the steak resting on the counter, heat a cast-iron skillet or heavy-bottomed pan over high heat.
  4. When the cooking surface is very hot and slightly smoking, carefully add a tablespoon of oil. It will likely splatter.
  5. Sear each side of the steaks for three to four minutes. For this dish, keep the meat medium-rare so it does not turn chewy.
  6. Transfer the steak to a cutting board to rest.

To cook the peppers and onions.

  1. Place a large clean skillet over medium-high heat.
  2. Pour a tablespoon of vegetable oil into the hot skillet. Add the onions and saute for about two minutes. Then add the sliced bell peppers and cook for another three minutes.
  3. Drain any liquid from the skillet and finish with the fresh lime juice. Stir, then remove the vegetables from the heat.

To serve the Chili’s Steak Fajitas recipe:

  1. Slice the rested beef into thin strips against the grain and set aside.
  2. Wrap the flour tortillas in a damp paper towel and microwave for 30 seconds. Serve warm.
  3. Set out bowls of shredded Colby-Jack cheese, sour cream, pico de Gallo, and lime wedges.
  4. Mix the sliced beef, any juices, and the sautéed vegetables and serve. (For the optional Chili-style sizzle plate) Heat a sizzle platter or clean cast-iron skillet for 4 minutes over high heat. Add a splash of water, then add the beef and vegetables. Serve immediately on a heatproof trivet.

What to serve this dish with

Make it a Chili’s night with a few of the other classic menu items from the chain.

Chili’s Pico de Gallo – Serve with chips for a starter or use as a topping for just about anything. Chili’s Pico de Gallo is fresh and flavorful. Made from juicy tomatoes, sharp onions, fresh cilantro, and diced jalapeños for a touch of heat, this simple dish is versatile and easy to make.

Chili’s Presidente Margarita – There’s nothing more refreshing than a margarita, and Chili’s Presidente Margarita is uniquely delicious. It combines tequila, brandy, and orange liqueur with sour mix for a tart and tasty cocktail that is just a little more sophisticated than most.

Chili’s Chocolate Brown Sundae – Cap your meal off with a Brownie Sundae. This recipe makes it easy by using a boxed brownie mix zhuzhed up with coarsely chopped walnuts. When they come out of the oven, cool for a few minutes, then top the still-warm brownies with vanilla ice cream, fudge sauce, and a maraschino cherry for an old-school dessert.

Storing and reheating instructions

Refrigerator Storage: Store the steak and the peppers and onions in separate airtight containers for up to 3 days. Keeping them separate prevents the vegetables from turning the beef soggy.

Reheating Method: Warm the peppers and onions in a hot skillet over medium-high heat for about 2 minutes, then add the beef and cook for 2 to 3 more minutes, until hot.

Freezer Storage: Not recommended. Skirt steak and sauteed peppers both lose texture significantly after freezing and thawing, turning stringy and watery.

Chili’s Copycat Steak Fajitas

Marinated skirt steak seared hot and served with sauteed peppers, onions, and all the classic fajita toppings.
Author: Stephanie Manley
PRINT PIN SAVE RECIPE SAVE RECIPE
No ratings yet
Servings : 6
Prep Time20 minutes minutes
Cook Time20 minutes minutes
Marinating2 hours hours
Total Time2 hours hours 40 minutes minutes

Ingredients
 

Steak

  • 2 pounds inside skirt steak
  • 3 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
  • 3 cloves garlic finely chopped
  • 2 teaspoons brown sugar

Peppers and Onions

  • 1 large sweet yellow onion
  • 1 red bell pepper sliced ½-inch
  • 1 green bell pepper sliced ½-inch
  • 1 orange bell pepper sliced ½-inch
  • 3 tablespoons neutral oil vegetable or avocado (Divided use)
  • 2 tablespoons water
  • 2 teaspoons soy sauce
  • 1 teaspoon Worcestershire added to vegetables while cooking
  • 1 teaspoon lime juice added at end of vegetable cook

For Serving

  • ½ cup shredded Colby-Jack cheese
  • ½ cup sour cream
  • ½ cup pico de gallo
  • flour tortillas

Instructions

  1. Marinate the Steak: In a bowl or large zip-top bag, combine the soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, fresh lime juice, chopped garlic, and brown sugar. Whisk or stir until the brown sugar is mostly dissolved.
  2. Add the skirt steak to the marinade, turning to coat it evenly. Seal the bag or cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight for the best flavor. Turn the steak halfway through marinating if possible.
  3. Prepare the Peppers and Onions: Slice the onion and bell peppers into ½-inch strips.
  4. In a separate bowl or zip-top bag, combine the neutral oil, water, soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce. Add the sliced onion and peppers, then toss until evenly coated. Let the vegetables marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.
  5. Cook the Steak: Remove the steak from the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking so it can warm up a bit. Remove it from the marinade and pat it completely dry with paper towels. Discard the used marinade.
  6. Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot and nearly smoking. Add 1 tablespoon of oil. Place the steak in the skillet and sear for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until a dark crust forms. Do not move the steak while it is searing.
  7. Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes. Slice it thinly against the grain before serving.
  8. Cook the Peppers and Onions: While the steak rests, heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a second skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 2 minutes. Add the bell peppers and cook for another 3 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender and lightly charred around the edges. Discard the vegetable marinade.
  9. Finish the vegetables with 1 teaspoon of lime juice and stir to combine. Remove from the heat.
  10. Serve the Fajitas: For sizzling service, heat a dry cast-iron skillet over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until very hot. Carefully add 2 tablespoons of water to the skillet. It will steam immediately. Add the sliced steak and cooked peppers and onions to the hot skillet and serve right away on a heat-proof trivet.
  11. Warm the flour tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for about 30 seconds.
  12. Serve the steak, peppers, and onions with warm tortillas, shredded Colby-Jack cheese, sour cream, pico de gallo, guacamole, and lime wedges.

Notes

  • Before marinating, trim any visible fat and silvery gristle from the skirt steak so the marinade can penetrate the meat directly. Skirt steak has long, visible muscle fibers running in one direction, so take note of that grain before it goes into the marinade. After cooking, you’ll slice against those fibers rather than parallel to them, which is what keeps the finished steak tender instead of stringy. 
  • Keep the steak at medium-rare. Skirt steak has looser muscle fibers than cuts like ribeye, and pushing it past medium turns it chewy fast.
  • Let the cast-iron skillet get properly hot and slightly smoking before the steak goes in. A cooler pan means the beef steams instead of searing, and you lose the browned crust.
  • The splash of water in the sizzle-platter step creates the audible sizzle and steam Chili’s is known for, but it’s purely presentation. Skip it and the dish tastes the same.
  • Resting the steak both before cooking (to room temperature) and after cooking (on the cutting board) matters just as much as the sear itself for a juicy result.
